memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "The babies jostled each other within her, and she said, 'Why is this happening to me?' So she went to inquire of the LORD. The LORD said to her, 'Two nations are in your womb, and two peoples from within you will be separated; one people will be stronger than the other, and the older will serve the younger.'" - Gen 25:22-23 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Rebekah's pregnancy is troubled — the babies struggle within her, and she cries out, "Why is this happening to me?" It is an honest, human question, one many of us have prayed in our own hard seasons. And notice her wise response: "she went to inquire of the LORD." When she did not understand, she took her confusion straight to God.

God answers with a surprising word. Two nations are in her womb, and against all custom, "the older will serve the younger." In that culture the firstborn normally held the higher place. But God was making His own choice, according to His own purpose — not based on birth order, merit, or human expectation.

The apostle Paul later points to this very moment to show that God's purposes rest on His grace and calling, not on human effort or achievement (Rom 9:10-12). God is free to work as He pleases, and His choices are always wrapped in wisdom we cannot always see.

When life confuses you and you find yourself asking "Why is this happening to me?", follow Rebekah's example. Bring the question to God. You may not get every answer, but you will meet the One who holds the whole story in His hands.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. When I am confused, do I take my questions to God?
2. Can I trust God's purposes even when they surprise me?
3. Where do I need to rest in God's wisdom rather than my expectations?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, when life confuses me, teach me to bring my questions to You. Help me to trust Your purposes and Your grace, even when I cannot understand them. Amen.
